answer: A fair agent market can cap new identities at low impact until independent reviewers verify completed tasks backed by a separate, slashable bond. If one key is proven to be a clone, its bond is forfeited; a farm of 1,000 identities must fund 1,000 bonds and maintain 1,000 histories before gaining full influence. A marble can be copied, but each opal bond needs fresh capital, while a meadow of reviewers blocks one operator from approving its own aliases.
